why_in_two_sentences: Our page defines the term precisely and then covers far more of the query's real subtopics (the two opposite directions, why steadiness feels dangerous, autophobia/BPD disambiguation, body sensations, working on it while single) than either competitor. Verywell Mind's only real advantages are cited statistics, a scannable up-front symptom list, and named therapy modalities; PsychCentral answers a slightly different query (abandonment trauma) rather than 'what is fear of abandonment.'

Verywell names specific therapy modalities as options (CBT, attachment-based therapy, behavioral therapy, play therapy for children)
Verywell explains 'object constancy' as a developmental mechanism, giving a concrete named concept for why the fear forms
Verywell includes a stage-by-stage walkthrough of how the fear plays out across a relationship's arc (getting to know, honeymoon, real relationship, the slight, the reactions)
Verywell cites numbered research/statistics (e.g., ~10% of US adults have a phobia), lending sourced authority
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Maps the two opposite strategies (bind-in/over-give vs never-arrive) and shows the same person runs both, with a behavior table (indispensable, monitoring, concealing, testing, leaving first, never arriving)
Explains why a calm/stable stretch feels more dangerous than conflict
Disambiguates the search intent explicitly: autophobia/monophobia vs abandonment, and that it is not a diagnosis and appears in but is not exclusive to BPD
Covers where it shows up outside romance (friends, family, work, own success, endings of any kind)
Gives concrete practice scripts for telling a partner without making reassurance their job, and for working on it while single
